_schema_note: V2. `slides` is now an array (2 or 3), because the unit is a carousel and the rant needs room. Slide 1 must open a loop, never carry half the joke. Last slide is always ink, all others paper.

rules_applied.hook_rule: Slide 1 is an instruction, a challenge or a claim that demands proof. If slide 1 can be screenshotted and understood alone, it has failed.
rules_applied.hinglish_ratio: 4 of 12 — code-switched the way people actually type, never decorative

posts.trend: 18% GST applies to the Merchant Discount Rate on UPI transactions above Rs 2,000 from 15 Oct 2026; P2P stays free.
posts.context: This cohort has paid for everything by UPI for a decade and treats it as free public infrastructure.
posts.angle: Follow a single note through one ordinary evening and count the tolls. Nothing has even been consumed yet.
slides: Follow one ₹100 through your day.

Salary credited — taxed.
Order dinner — taxed.
Delivery fee — taxed.
Platform fee — taxed.

From 15 October, paying for it — taxed.

You still haven't eaten.
posts.caption: Eleven years of free UPI and they found the last free thing. Tag someone who still says "UPI kar dena".

posts.trend: Indian IT firms tightened RTO in 2026 — Infosys' attendance app auto-rejects WFH below 10 office days a month; TCS ties presence to variable pay; Wipro mandates 6 hours across 3 days.
posts.context: People moved cities, took flats further out and moved parents in, on the strength of these promises.
posts.angle: The company never deleted the promise. It just stopped honouring it, and left the evidence online.
slides: Go and read your company's 2021 LinkedIn post again.

"Work from anywhere."
"Flexibility is the future."
"We trust our people."
"Remote-first. Forever."

In 2026 an app auto-rejects your WFH if you missed ten office days.

The post is still up.
posts.caption: Nobody took it down. That's the part that gets me.

posts.trend: Evergreen — the Indian family's most-used word.
posts.context: "Settle ho ja" is said to every Indian adult, by everyone, permanently.
posts.angle: It is not a destination. It is a moving target, and it has never once been reached by anybody.
slides: There is a word your family uses that has no fixed meaning.

"Settle ho ja."

At 22 it meant a job.
At 26 it meant a flat.
At 30 it means a wedding.
At 34 it will mean a child.

Nobody in your family has ever been settled.

It just moves.
posts.caption: Ask the person telling you to settle whether they have settled. Watch what happens.

posts.trend: Evergreen — the universal Indian coping instruction.
posts.context: Every structural problem in an Indian life is answered with the same two words.
posts.angle: Adjustment was sold as resilience. Thirty years of it is not resilience, it is deformation.
slides: Indian families have one patch for every bug in the system.

Low salary? Thoda adjust kar lo.
Bad manager? Thoda adjust kar lo.
Terrible flat? Thoda adjust kar lo.
Wrong marriage? Thoda adjust kar lo.

Thirty years of adjusting.

You are now shaped like the problem.
posts.caption: "Adjust kar lo" has done more damage than any recession.

posts.trend: India's economy grew 7.8% in the April-June 2026 quarter.
posts.context: Appraisals in Indian offices are running 4-8% while the headline number is quoted back at employees as good news.
posts.angle: You are inside the growth. You are receiving none of it.
slides: The economy grew 7.8% this quarter.

Your rent grew 10%.
Your grocery bill grew.
Your parents' expectations grew.
Your salary is "under review".
Congratulations to the economy.
posts.caption: Genuinely thrilled for it.

posts.trend: Bengaluru IT-corridor rents rising 8-15% in 2026; Mumbai 8-12%; two-three month deposits plus a month of brokerage standard.
posts.context: Renting has stopped being a stopgap for this cohort and become the permanent arrangement.
posts.angle: Your landlord runs a faster, more confident compensation cycle than your employer.
slides: Your landlord runs a better appraisal process than your company.

No self-assessment form.
No calibration meeting.
No "budget constraints this year".
No "let's revisit in Q3".

One WhatsApp message in October. 10%. Confirmed.
posts.caption: He doesn't even know your rating. Incredible conviction.

posts.trend: Evergreen — the sentences that keep an Indian adult's life running.
posts.context: A shared, unspoken script that every 30-year-old uses daily without thinking.
posts.angle: These aren't lies to other people. They are a maintenance protocol.
slides: The four sentences holding your life together.

"Bas nikal hi raha hoon."
"Haan haan, kha liya."
"Kal se gym."
"Main dekh leta hoon."

You have used all four today.

Two were to your mother.
posts.caption: "Bas 5 minute" — a man who has not left the bed.

posts.trend: IMD warned of extremely heavy rainfall across Chhattisgarh, eastern MP, UP and the Northeast in mid-September 2026; Kolkata saw waterlogging and traffic disruption.
posts.context: RTO mandates and monsoon commutes are colliding at full scale for the first time.
posts.angle: Infrastructure is allowed to fail. You are not.
slides: It rained for forty minutes this morning.

The main road is a river.
The auto wants ₹400 for 3 km.
The metro has become a single organism.
Your manager has sent "standup in 10?"

The city stopped.

The 9:30 did not.
posts.caption: "Plan your commute accordingly" — a company, to a person who cannot swim.

posts.trend: Festival season 2026: Navratri from 11 Oct, Durga Puja 16-21 Oct, Dussehra 20 Oct, Diwali 8 Nov.
posts.context: The first stretch of the year where being the earning adult of the family is fully itemised.
posts.angle: Childhood festivals were received. Adult festivals are budgeted.
slides: Festival season starts in three weeks. Open your calculator.

Flights home: two.
Gifts: eleven, minimum.
Sweets for the office: ₹1,400.
Cash for the kids at home: unknown, always more than planned.

At 12 you counted what you got.

At 30 you count what it cost.
posts.caption: Book now. The fare only moves one way.

posts.trend: Evergreen — the daily check-in with an Indian mother.
posts.context: Financial independence changes nothing about the script.
posts.angle: You run an entire household and still file a daily report you cannot pass.
slides:
You run a house and manage a team.

Here is your daily performance review.

"Khana kha liya?"
"Haan."
"Kya khaya?"
"...khana."

Thirty years old.

Still negotiating.
posts.caption: Maggi at 11:40pm is technically khana. Technically.

posts.context: This cohort's first encounter with injuries that have no origin story.
posts.angle: Pain used to be earned. Now it just arrives.
slides: List every injury you currently have. Go on.

Neck — from sleeping.
Back — from sitting.
Knee — from standing up once.
Wrist — unknown, since March.

Not one of them has a story.

That's the part nobody warns you about.
posts.caption: At 22 the injuries at least came with a night out.

posts.trend: West Indies tour India from 27 Sep 2026 — three ODIs and five T20Is.
posts.context: Cricket was the shared language of this cohort's childhood; the fixture volume has outgrown anyone's attention.
posts.angle: You didn't lose interest. There is simply more cricket than a life has room for.
slides: A series starts on Saturday. You found out from a meme.

At 15 you knew every batting average.
At 22 you knew the playing XI.
At 26 you knew the captain.
At 30 you know there is cricket happening.
There is always cricket happening.
posts.caption: Somewhere, right now, India is playing someone. That's the whole update.

cut.text: Papa never calls / Papa asks Mummy to ask you...
cut.reason: Cut on review — the observation is true but it is warm, not satirical, and the payoff is a shrug rather than a landing.

rejected_demo.trend: Nepal flood death toll crosses 1,000; rescue teams working in remote areas.
rejected_demo.reason: Active mass-casualty disaster. The gate rejects any trend whose subject is death, violence, communal conflict or a named private individual — before the content agent ever sees it.

audit.escalating_list: 6/12 (50%) — OVER the 30% cap, acceptable only for a seed set; the generator must diversify
